title: The Challenge of the Invisible Thread
summary: A foreign weaver claims to have woven a garment of invisible silk that only the truly wise can see. Birbal outsmarts the fraud with his own invisible reward.
keywords: the challenge of the invisible thread
full_text:
A smooth-talking merchant-weaver named Zafar arrived at the imperial court of Fatehpur Sikri, carrying a locked mahogany chest. Bowing low before Emperor Akbar, the weaver made an extraordinary claim:

'Your Imperial Majesty! After thirty years of secret experiments, I have woven a fabric of celestial silk. It is lighter than air, softer than rose petals, and possessing one miraculous quality: it is completely invisible to fools, liars, and corrupt men! Only the purest souls and the truly wise can behold its breathtaking colors!'

The weaver unlocked the chest, pantomimed opening a bundle of cloth, and held his empty hands high in the air:

'Behold, Your Majesty! See the magnificent golden embroidery, the deep crimson weave, the emerald borders!'

Akbar looked at the weaver's hands. He saw nothing but empty air!

Akbar's heart sank in private panic: 'Can it be that I am a fool or an unworthy emperor? I cannot see the cloth!'

Not wishing to appear foolish, Akbar nodded solemnly: 'Magnificent! Truly a masterpiece of the weaver's craft!'

The courtiers, observing the Emperor's praise and terrified of being branded fools or traitors, fell over each other to praise the invisible fabric: 'Incredible! Look at those sapphires! What divine craftsmanship!'

Only Birbal stood quietly with a faint smirk.

The weaver smiled greedily: 'Since Your Majesty appreciates this celestial fabric, I shall tailor a royal robe for the upcoming coronation parade. The cost is merely ten thousand gold mohurs.'

Akbar ordered the gold paid. Two weeks later, the weaver returned, pretending to carry a magnificent robe over his arms. He went through the motions of helping Akbar undress and 'dressing' the monarch in the invisible robe.

Akbar stood in his undergarments, feeling completely naked and absurd, yet afraid to speak. 'Birbal,' Akbar whispered nervously, 'how does the robe look upon me?'

Birbal bowed with the utmost seriousness: 'Sire, the robe is breathtaking! The craftsmanship is beyond words! And to reward this master weaver properly, I have brought his payment.'

Birbal opened a velvet pouch, reached his hand inside, pulled out empty air, and began counting 'coins' into the weaver's open palms:

'Here is one thousand invisible gold coins, two thousand, three thousand... exactly ten thousand celestial gold mohurs!'

The weaver stood frozen, his empty hands cupped. 'My lord, there is nothing in my hands!'

Birbal's eyes flashed with triumphant humor:

'What? Do you not see the pure gold? Ah, forgive me! I forgot to mention—these celestial gold coins were minted in heaven! They are completely invisible to swindlers, cheats, and liars! Only the honest can see and spend them!'

The weaver turned pale as a sheet. Realizing his fraud had been completely exposed, he fell upon his knees, returned the real gold treasury advance, and begged for mercy. Akbar laughed till tears flowed and commended Birbal for saving the throne from public ridicule.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
